=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:180-181 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: The self-triggered autofix skip check is unreachable because `EVENT_NAME` is compared to `pull_request`, but this reusable workflow is invoked via `workflow_call` or `workflow_dispatch` so that value never matches in the called workflow.
  WHY: All reviewers identified the same root cause; one reviewer called this critical while others marked it high, so the consensus severity uses the highest reported level.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:182-182 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: The `AUTOFIX_SKIP_SELF_TRIGGERED` flag is compared with a case-sensitive literal `false`, so non-lowercase variants do not disable the skip.
  WHY: Both reviewers described the same boolean-handling bug at the same check, with one noting the broader implication that uppercase or mixed-case values remain truthy.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:185-188 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: The empty `bot_login` guard can silently disable the skip logic when the bot login variable resolves to an empty string.
  WHY: Single-reviewer finding preserved unchanged.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:190-197 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: The `gh api ... @tsv` output is parsed with `cut`, which can corrupt the extracted commit metadata if fields contain tab characters.
  WHY: All three reviewers reported the same fragile TSV parsing root cause on overlapping line ranges, with one reviewer rating it lower confidence than the others.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:3854-3863 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: The post-commit retrigger guard exits early, preventing the workflow from continuing into retrigger logic after a commit.
  WHY: Reviewers agreed the `exit 0` ends the flow prematurely; one reviewer framed the impact as stalling the autofix loop, while another noted it also bypasses later retrigger checks.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:3858-3860 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3-flash-preview]
  PROBLEM: The hard `exit 0` stops the workflow before any later retrigger logic in that step can run.
  WHY: Single-reviewer finding preserved unchanged.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:194-196 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: The TSV parsing can split on tabs embedded in commit messages and shift the extracted fields.
  WHY: Single-reviewer finding preserved unchanged.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:195-197 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3-flash-preview]
  PROBLEM: The `cut`-based TSV parsing can misalign if any field contains a tab character.
  WHY: Single-reviewer finding preserved unchanged.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:190-195 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2]
  PROBLEM: Parsing GitHub API JSON output as TSV with `cut` is brittle and can break on tab characters in commit messages.
  WHY: Single-reviewer finding preserved unchanged.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v3_2 ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:180 (condition `[ "${EVENT_NAME}" = "pull_request" ]`) | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: In a reusable workflow (`workflow_call`), `github.event_name` evaluates to `workflow_call`, not the original event name from the caller.
  WHY: This makes the self-triggered autofix skip completely non-functional when invoked through wrapper workflows.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:180 (condition `[ "${AUTOFIX_SKIP_SELF_TRIGGERED:-true}" != "false" ]`) | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Boolean check is case-sensitive; uppercase `FALSE` or other variants do not disable the skip as users would intuitively expect.
  WHY: Repository variables set as `FALSE`, `False`, or other case variations will not match the literal string `"false"`, causing the skip to remain active when the user intended to disable it.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:3854-3860 (post-commit retrigger guard `exit 0`) | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When combined with a non-functional gate skip, this guard prevents the `workflow_dispatch` that would continue the autofix loop, potentially stalling multi‑iteration fixes.
  WHY: If the gate skip fails (primary issue), the full verification run executes. The post-commit guard then skips the retrigger dispatch with `exit 0`, leaving no automatic follow-up. The autofix loop deadlocks—the current run finishes but no new iteration is dispatched.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:190-195 (TSV parsing with `cut`) | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: Parsing GitHub API JSON output as TSV with `cut` assumes no tab characters in commit messages and perfectly formatted fields.
  WHY: A commit message containing a tab character would cause `cut -f1` to capture only the substring before the first tab, potentially mis‑identifying the commit prefix. Edge‑case API responses could also break the field alignment.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v3_2 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3-flash-preview ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:180 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The gate's skip check for self-triggered autofixes is likely unreachable in many repository configurations because `EVENT_NAME` is checked for an exact match of `pull_request`.
  WHY: When this workflow is called as a reusable workflow (common in this repository's "internal" and "consumer" patterns via `workflow_call`), `github.event_name` (assigned to `EVENT_NAME`) returns `workflow_call`, not `pull_request`.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:3858-3860 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The post-commit retrigger guard uses a hard `exit 0`, which stops the workflow from executing any subsequent retrigger logic.
  WHY: While this correctly skips the immediate `workflow_dispatch` for that PR, it also bypasses the `autofix_retrigger_has_inflight_peer` check and any other future retrigger logic that might be added to this step.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:195-197 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Parsing the TSV API output using `cut` without a specified delimiter defaults to any whitespace, but `gh api ... | @tsv` produces literal tab characters that can be problematic if the message itself contains tabs.
  WHY: If a commit message (or any field) contains a tab character, the `cut -f1` logic misaligns, potentially causing the `head_msg_line` to be truncated or contain part of the login fields.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3-flash-preview ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:~174-176 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The gate job checks `EVENT_NAME == "pull_request"` but this workflow is triggered only by `workflow_call` and `workflow_dispatch`, so the skip mechanism never activates.
  WHY: The wrapper workflow receives the `pull_request` event and invokes this reusable workflow via `workflow_call`, which means `github.event_name` inside this workflow will be `workflow_call`, never `pull_request`.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:~3859-3863 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: After a successful autofix commit, the post-commit retrigger step exits with code 0 without dispatching the next workflow.
  WHY: The autofix loop stops here and waits for the stall cron or an external event, so the intended multi-iteration flow does not continue automatically.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:~175, ~1859 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The `AUTOFIX_SKIP_SELF_TRIGGERED` comparison only recognizes the literal lowercase string `"false"` as falsy.
  WHY: Values like `"FALSE"`, `"False"`, `"0"`, `"True"`, and `"1"` are treated as truthy, which is inconsistent with typical boolean handling.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:~185-188 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The `bot_login` guard silently disables the skip logic when the bot login value is empty.
  WHY: If `AUTOFIX_BOT_LOGIN` is empty or resolves unexpectedly to an empty string, the comparison cannot run and the user gets no warning.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:180-181 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The self-triggered autofix skip check is unreachable because `review_autofix.yml` is only invoked via `workflow_call` from wrapper workflows.
  WHY: When invoked via `workflow_call`, `github.event_name` is `workflow_call`, not `pull_request`, so the condition `EVENT_NAME="pull_request"` can never be true.
=== END FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM stepfun_step-3_5-flash ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:180 (gate evaluate step: `[ "${EVENT_NAME}" = "pull_request" ]`) | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The self-triggered autofix skip gating logic checks EVENT_NAME against "pull_request", but this reusable workflow only declares `workflow_call` and `workflow_dispatch` triggers.
  WHY: Inside a `workflow_call`, `github.event_name` is `workflow_call`, never `pull_request`, making this condition unreachable.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:182 (gate step) and 3854 (post-commit retrigger step) | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The boolean flag AUTOFIX_SKIP_SELF_TRIGGERED is compared to the literal "false" using case-sensitive string equality.
  WHY: Only lowercase "false" disables the skip; values like "FALSE", "False", or "FaLsE" are treated as truthy and keep the skip enabled.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:194-196 (within the gate skip block) | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The TSV output from `gh api ... --jq '[...] | @tsv'` is parsed using `cut`, which can corrupt the extracted commit metadata if fields contain tab characters.
  WHY: If a commit message contains a tab, `cut` will split on that tab and shift field boundaries, returning corrupted values for the commit subject line, author login, and committer login.
=== END FINDINGS FROM stepfun_step-3_5-flash ===
